title: Lazur vs Superwhisper on Mac: offline dictation or an assistant that sees your screen
metaTitle: Lazur vs Superwhisper: which one fits your Mac
description: Lazur vs Superwhisper for Mac: offline, tunable dictation or a voice assistant that sees your screen and dictates. Real prices from each company's site.
intro: Superwhisper is dictation with local and cloud models, including offline transcription. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac: it dictates, and it also sees your screen, answers out loud and points at buttons.
tldr: Superwhisper is a dictation tool. Lazur is a voice assistant that also dictates.
Pick Superwhisper if typing by voice is all you need, on more devices.
Pick Lazur if you also want help with what is on your screen: answers, pointing at buttons, step-by-step guidance.
Lazur is free for 3 days, then $18/month.

blocks.text: Superwhisper is about getting your words onto the page, on your terms; Lazur is about getting help with the app you are in.

faq.question: Is Lazur a good Superwhisper alternative?
faq.answer: If you want more than dictation, yes. Lazur dictates in any Mac app and also answers questions about your screen, points at buttons and guides you. If you only dictate, Superwhisper is a fine choice.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur and Superwhisper together?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as their shortcuts do not clash. Lazur uses hold fn to dictate and hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask.

faq.question: Does Lazur work offline like Superwhisper?
faq.answer: No. Lazur sends audio and one screenshot to AI providers while you hold the shortcut, and nothing is stored. Superwhisper offers offline models.
